title: Add a JPG as the Last Page of a PDF on iPhone
description: Append a JPG to a PDF on iPhone. Convert the photo to one PDF page, merge it after the original, and verify the last page before sharing.
direct: Turn the JPG into a one-page PDF, then merge it after the original document. Open the result and check the last page before sending it.
figureAlt: A three-page paper packet with a photo-only last page
figureCaption: AI-generated illustration. The image page belongs after the report in this example. The illustration shows page order.
cards.decision.heading: Make the photo a page first
cards.decision.body: A JPEG attached to a message remains its own file. Turn it into a page when the recipient needs one document with the supporting image in a known position.
sections.detail-1.heading: Check the image at reading size
sections.detail-1.body: A photo can look fine in a thumbnail while small writing is too soft to read on a PDF page. Zoom in to check the details the recipient needs, such as a timestamp or a label. If they are unreadable, make a better source image before merging again.
sections.detail-2.heading: Check special document requirements
sections.detail-2.body: Merging can affect interactive fields or digital signature validation. If an original signature must remain valid, ask whether the recipient will accept the original and the photo as separate files.
faqs.reader-1.heading: Can I add two images at the end?
faqs.reader-1.body: Make a PDF of the images, check their sequence, then append it after the report.
faqs.reader-2.heading: Will merging improve photo quality?
faqs.reader-2.body: The detail comes from your original JPG. Use a clearer photo if the page is difficult to read.

steps.step-1.text: Save the JPG and the original PDF in Files. Check that the image is upright and all relevant details are visible.
steps.step-2.text: In PDF Compressor: Sign & Merge, use JPG to PDF to create a one-page PDF from the image. Save it with a name you can recognize at merge time.
steps.step-3.text: Use Merge PDFs with the report first and the image page second. Save a separate merged file. Open it and check the total page count and the last page.
